editorialCapacityRationale: The Stockholm museum presents about 5,000 objects in a chronological six-century route and combines paintings, sculpture, drawings, prints, applied arts and design. A 40-item planning capacity is large enough to cover the main media, periods and collection logic without treating the wider 700,000-plus-object institutional collection or off-site venues as one visitable museum.

collectionBoundaries.physicalScope: Nationalmuseum Stockholm at Södra Blasieholmshamnen 2 on Blasieholmen, including the publicly accessible permanent collection presentations in the main building: the Timeline galleries, the Design Depot, the Treasury and the Sculpture Courtyard. The run is about the Stockholm visitor experience and its on-site collection presentation, not the entire Nationalmuseum authority or every place where its holdings are displayed.

includedSites.name: Nationalmuseum Stockholm
includedSites.candidatePoolRule: Include objects from the permanent Stockholm presentations or objects whose official Nationalmuseum record gives a clear main-building presentation context; do not infer current display from collection ownership alone.

includedCollectionGroups.name: Paintings and sculptures
includedCollectionGroups.scope: Renaissance/early modern material through around 1900, with the Stockholm galleries emphasizing Swedish and European art across the chronological route.

includedCollectionGroups.name: Drawings and prints
includedCollectionGroups.scope: Nationalmuseum's graphic-art holdings from the late Middle Ages to 1900, included only when a work has a documented visitor-facing Stockholm presentation or a clearly relevant on-site collection context.

includedCollectionGroups.name: Applied arts, design and industrial design
includedCollectionGroups.scope: From the late Middle Ages/14th century through the present, including ceramics, textiles, glass, metalwork, furniture and books where represented in the Stockholm presentations.

includedCollectionGroups.name: Portraits
includedCollectionGroups.scope: Portraits represented in the Stockholm collection presentation; the separate National Portrait Gallery at Gripsholm is outside this run.

collectionBoundaries.institutionalBoundary: Nationalmuseum is both a museum and a Swedish government authority. This run treats the Stockholm museum building and its visitor-facing collection presentation as the museum scope, while retaining the wider institutional collection groups only to define exclusions and prevent cross-site mixing.

exclusions.name: National Portrait Gallery at Gripsholm Castle
exclusions.reason: Separate off-site venue in Gripsholm; not part of a Stockholm museum visit.

exclusions.name: Royal Castles collections at Gripsholm, Drottningholm, Strömsholm, Rosersberg and Ulriksdal
exclusions.reason: Separate palace and castle locations with their own access and display contexts; exclude from the Stockholm candidate pool.

exclusions.name: Gustavsberg collection and Gustavsberg Porcelain Museum
exclusions.reason: Separate collection and museum site at Gustavsberg; exclude even though the collection is managed within the wider Nationalmuseum institution.

exclusions.name: Nationalmuseum Jamtli in Östersund
exclusions.reason: Separate off-site exhibition venue; exclude from the Stockholm run.

exclusions.name: The Tessin Institute's art collection at the Swedish Institute in Paris
exclusions.reason: Separate international collection/display site; exclude from a Stockholm visit.

exclusions.name: Läckö Castle and other external exhibition locations
exclusions.reason: Nationalmuseum collection displays outside the Stockholm building are separate locations and may have independent dates or access conditions.

exclusions.name: Temporary exhibitions, temporary gallery displays and incoming loans
exclusions.reason: Time-limited programming and loans are not stable collection scope; they are excluded from the canonical collection candidate pool.

exclusions.name: Archives, art library, study room and research resources as standalone works
exclusions.reason: These are research or appointment contexts rather than the ordinary public collection route; they may be referenced later only when an object has an explicit visitor-facing presentation.

exclusions.name: Long-term loans and works held at government offices, residences, embassies or other borrowers
exclusions.reason: Institutional holdings outside the Stockholm visitor route are not assumed to be viewable at Nationalmuseum.

sourcePointers.title: Getting here
sourcePointers.supports: The museum's Stockholm location on Blasieholmen, the visiting address Södra Blasieholmshamnen 2, and the fact that this is the primary Stockholm visitor site.

sourcePointers.title: About Nationalmuseum
sourcePointers.supports: Institutional identity as Sweden's museum of art and design, its government-authority status, and the broad chronology/media boundary of paintings, sculptures, drawings, prints, applied arts, design and portraits.

sourcePointers.title: The collections
sourcePointers.supports: The official collection groups and their scope: approximately 16,000 paintings and sculptures, about 30,000 applied-arts/design objects, 500,000 prints and drawings, the National Portrait Gallery and Royal Castles collections, the Gustavsberg collection, and the Tessin Institute collection.

sourcePointers.title: Visit
sourcePointers.supports: The ordinary visitor-facing Stockholm scope: art and design from the 16th century to the present, about 5,000 objects presented chronologically, and arts, crafts and design displayed together.

sourcePointers.title: What is currently on display in the museum galleries?
sourcePointers.supports: The on-site gallery boundary and stable collection presentation: numbered galleries on the top and middle floors, chronological periods from the 16th century onward, the Treasury, and the separation of temporary galleries.

sourcePointers.title: Exhibitions
sourcePointers.supports: The distinction between the Stockholm collection presentations and temporary exhibitions, plus the separate list of exhibitions at other locations including Östersund, Gustavsberg, Läckö Castle, Paris and other venues.
